gateSources.Moerenpoort: survives (1379); inventory 37296; Ferraris 'Porte du Pont'; also called Visépoort

walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tongeren' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140056)
walls.note: Tongeren medieval wall (c. 1290, about 2.7 km, six gates; enlarged early 16th c.), traced from the Ferraris map (1777). The 2nd-c. Roman wall (4.5 km) ran further out and stood partly as ruins in 1650 (pois). Local metres around the Grote Markt.

landmarks.y1650: Collegiate church of Our Lady (Gothic, 13th-16th c.) with its 64 m west tower finished in 1541, the main bell tower of Tongeren; with cloister.
Gate of 1379 on the Jeker side, the only surviving gate (also called Visépoort).
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tongeren' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140056); id.erfgoed.net 37296

landmarks.y1650: Remains of the 2nd-c. Roman town wall (4.5 km), far outside the medieval wall on the south and west; partly standing as ruin in 1650. Position: the Ferraris map labels it 'Remparts Romains'.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tongeren' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140056)

landmarks.y1650: Beguinage moved inside the walls in 1257 (early Gothic church).
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tongeren' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140056)

landmarks.y1650: Cloth hall mentioned in 1250; position not verified (the present town hall is of 1737-53).

ruler.name: Prinsbisdom Luik
ruler.sovereign: Prince-bishop Ferdinand of Bavaria (1612-50), then Maximilian Henry of Bavaria (elected 1650); neutral in the Franco-Spanish war (neutrality recognised by Spain only in 1654, see history-check F76)
